result.response:
**All 9 tests pass** (`# fail 0`). The three failures had independent root causes:

**1. `packages/cli/src/flags.js`** — flag values were stored as-is, so `--port 8080` gave the string `"8080"` instead of the number `8080`. A `// TODO: numbers stay strings` comment marked the known gap. Now numeric values are coerced with `/^\d+$/.test(next) ? Number(next) : next`, so string flags like `--name Ada` still work. (`src/index.js` passes this straight to `.listen()`, so the number coercion also fixes the port there.)

**2. `packages/shared/src/dates.js`** — `dayKey` used local-time getters (`getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate`) although the doc comment and test name both say "UTC days". The test sets `TZ=America/New_York`, where `2026-01-02T02:30:00Z` is still Jan 1 local, yielding `"2026-01-01"`. Switched to the `getUTC*` variants — the correct fix regardless of host timezone, which is what "group events by calendar day in UTC" requires.

**3. `packages/shared/src/format.js`** — `displayName` did `user.name.trim()` with no guard, throwing `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'name')` for both `displayName(null)` and `displayName({})`. Now uses optional chaining and falls back to `"anonymous"`, which also covers a whitespace-only name.

Two incidental notes, not part of this fix: `packages/api/src/server.js:44` has its own documented unhandled-rejection bug for malformed JSON bodies (no test covers it), and `server.js:37` has a `TODO: check that the user exists` — both out of scope here but worth a follow-up.

**2. `packages/shared/src/dates.js`** — `dayKey()` used local-time getters (`getDate()`, etc.) despite the doc comment saying days are grouped "in UTC".
